metadata.title: Comparative analysis of the Upwork MCP manual and three profile-overhaul plans
metadata.subject_profile: Aryan P., Top Rated, 100% Job Success, https://www.upwork.com/freelancers/~01c405f48e970fd854
metadata.verification_limit: Live Upwork pages were not re-opened in this session. Counts, rates, contract history, and Job Success wording are taken from the four files, which say they were read on 2026-10-04. Where those files conflict, confirm the live account before acting.

verdict.adopt: UPWORK_OVERHAUL_PLAN_v2_by_claude.xml is the plan to follow.
verdict.use_as: UPWORK_MCP_DOCUMENTATION.xml is the operating manual for search, vetting, drafting, and human confirmation. It is not a business plan.
verdict.direction_only: UPWORK_OVERHAUL_PLAN_by_claude.xml has the right direction and the wrong prices. Treat it as superseded by v2 except where this analysis says v2 still overreaches.
verdict.reject_as_profile_strategy: upwork_strategy_overhaul_by_Gemini.xml should not be used as the profile strategy.
verdict.summary: Reputation is already strong. The funnel is off, the catalog points at OpenClaw, and the $120 profile rate sits above almost every posted ceiling and far above the visible hourly history. Sell Claude setup for business teams as fixed-price packages, start every new client with a small milestone, and use the MCP server only to find and draft proposals that a human confirms.

document.what_it_is: A tool manual for Upwork's official MCP server: 51 tools, OAuth 2.1, and a draft-then-confirm gate.

what_it_suggests.point: Nothing is submitted and no Connects are spent until upwork__confirm_preview is called with a server-issued preview_id.

Discovery uses find_jobs smart_search with mode most_recent, days_posted 1, and verified_payment_only. That is the only search mode described as supporting a real date filter. Title search is preferred over a loose query. A low proposal count (the manual's alternative search uses a max around 10) is the competition filter.
Before drafting, open the job, then check invitations and existing proposals so manage_proposals create does not hit error VJ-JA-10.
Default vetting prefers lifetime spend over $1,000, hire rate over 50%, and flags client ratings below 4.6. Discard a single-seat job if someone is already hired.
Cover letters may use names found in client feedback. Boost only when the preview recommends it and the bid meets the recommended floor without exceeding the balance ceiling.
Accepting a contract offer cannot be finished in MCP. It returns a finalize_url for a human signature on upwork.com.

document.what_it_is: A market-driven repositioning away from OpenClaw toward Claude implementation, with a done-for-you ladder and a DIY kit treated as a bonus.

what_it_suggests.point: The problem is activity and positioning, not reputation: 0 recent proposals, 0 profile views in 7 days, availability badge off, about $2,172 earned in 12 months, against Top Rated, 100% Job Success, 35 jobs, and $20K+ earned.

OpenClaw has about 24 jobs in two quarters. Jobs with Claude in the title number roughly 300 to 350, about 10 new per day. MCP-server searches are too thin to be a headline (about 8 jobs in 2 months at a serious budget).
Premium AI posts fill up (often 20 to 50+ proposals in a few days). The workable pocket is setup, training, coaching, audits, and tool-specific integrations.
Drop the profile rate from $120 to about $85. Lead with fixed price. Raise the sticker after every three completed contracts at the current level.

Offers: Claude Setup Sprint $299 to $1,200, AI Operations Audit $750 to $1,500, implementation $3,000 to $7,500 only after a small first milestone, care plan $1,000 to $2,500 per month, coaching $100 to $150 per hour or $750 per workshop.
Remove the "over 8 years" claim and the "100% GxP/HIPAA" guarantee. One profile, one promise. Portfolio must show Claude work, not only 2023 chatbots.
Send 4 to 6 vetted proposals a day on jobs under 15 proposals and under 24 hours old. Past clients are the highest-probability path in week one.

A signed contract inside 7 days can be realistic. Cash in the bank inside 7 days is not, because of Upwork's payment hold. DIY pack revenue without an audience is not supported; plan on $0 to $300 a month and use the kit as a delivery asset.

document.what_it_is: The same strategy as v1, corrected with exact marketplace counts, a lower rate, competitor history, average-hourly-paid vetting, and Job Success weights read from the insights page.

what_it_suggests.point: Proposals: 0 in the last 7 days, last activity about 3 months ago. v1's "0 in the last 3 months" statistic is corrected.

313 open jobs with Claude in the title (215 hourly, 98 fixed). Only 46 hourly jobs allow $50 or more. Only 9 allow $100 or more. Of the fixed-price jobs, 40 are under $100, 34 are $100 to $500, 10 are $500 to $1,000, 9 are $1,000 to $5,000, and 5 are over $5,000. About 67% already have 20 or more proposals. Only 9 have fewer than 5 proposals.
Related pools: 404 jobs with "AI agent" in the title, 204 with n8n, 24 for OpenClaw, 8 for a serious "MCP server" budget.

Set the profile rate to about $65, twice the highest visible hourly rate of $30 and inside the ceiling of the better-paying Claude jobs. Earn a high effective rate through packages: a $599 sprint delivered in a few hours is a high hourly equivalent without showing that rate.
Visible hourly history includes $3, $5, $12, $20, $25, and $30. No visible hourly contract is above $30. The $120 sticker is about four times the highest visible hourly rate.

Total spend misleads. One full post from a client with $430K spent and a 4.75 rating pays an average of $5.04 per hour. Another, $245K spent, rating 4.99, pays about $41.87 per hour and is the shape of a good small first engagement.

South Asian competitors who have earned the most in this search list $10 to $35 per hour. Freelancers listed around $90 to $100 lead with an outcome or a certification, then expand from small fixed jobs. One public history (Andrew W.) shows tutoring and builds from a few hundred dollars, a $1,000 audit, then a $10,400 engagement with one agency.

Job Success, as read from the insights page: a job of $251 or more counts as 1.25, a job of $1,001 or more counts as 1.5 and is capped, and a client whose latest payment is more than 90 days after the first can make jobs with that client count as successful. Five open contracts from 2023 and 2024, plus a repeat enterprise client, are flagged for reactivation. v2 says to confirm the 90-day reading on one client first.
Gumroad lists 815 products for "claude skills"; among top results, ratings are 0 to 6 and many are free. Build the kit as a delivery toolkit and a free sample, not as income.

Add an Automation Rescue offer at $499 to $1,500. Keep implementation at $3,000 to $7,500 only for clients who already finished a sprint or audit. Daily volume is 3 to 5 proposals, Connects cap about 80 per day.
Anthropic's Claude Certified Architect exam is cited at $125, but only people at Claude Partner Network organizations can sit it. Confirm before planning around it.

document.what_it_is: A high-ticket repositioning as an Enterprise AI Architect, with MCP servers and multi-agent systems as the product.

what_it_suggests.point: Keep the published rate at $120 to $150. Set a contract floor of $3,000. Anchor value on fixed architecture milestones of $3,500 or more.
Headline: Enterprise AI Architect | Custom MCP Servers, LangGraph and Autonomous Multi-Agent Systems.
Turn consultations on at $150 for 45 minutes. The file says consultations are currently off.
Catalog: an MCP boilerplate at $199 to $499 delivered in 1 day, a custom MCP server at $1,500 to $4,000 in 4 days, and a feasibility audit at $299.
A second funnel sells DIY kits at $149 to $499 and expects catalog cash in 24 to 48 hours. High-ticket cash is projected 5 to 7 days from consultation to funded milestone.
Overview copy promises enterprise-grade infrastructure, OAuth 2.1 MCP servers, LangGraph and CrewAI, and zero-leakage local LLM and RAG systems for healthcare, legal, and enterprise compliance.
Client filters: rating at least 4.8, historical spend at least $1,000, decline open-ended briefs under $200. Seven-day plan assumes catalog orders and a $3,500 to $6,000 upsell by day six.

agreements.point: The diagnosis is right. This is an activity and positioning problem. Top Rated and 100% Job Success are already in place.
OpenClaw should come off the catalog. Two of three listings point at a keyword with about 24 jobs.

The work to sell is Claude setup for a team: Claude Code or Cowork, a few custom skills, connectors into tools they already use, a short recording, and a written handover. Audits and rescue of a broken build sit next to that.
Custom MCP servers are a line inside that offer. They are not the headline. Both Claude plans and the MCP manual's market note put serious "MCP server" demand at about 8 jobs in two months.

Fixed-price packages are how to get paid like a high hourly freelancer while the profile still shows a $30 history. A $599 sprint done in a short engagement is a high effective rate without asking a stranger to believe a $120 sticker.
Every new client starts with a small paid milestone. The recent Job Success base is 8 eligible jobs. A large first build with a new client is the risk.

Vet average hourly rate paid, the reviews the client leaves, hire rate, whether someone is already hired, and whether the post allows your location. The $430K spent / $5.04 per hour example is the strongest finding in the set. Lifetime spend over $1,000, which the MCP manual uses as a default, is too weak alone.

Remove claims a buyer can check and doubt: "over 8 years" next to a 2017–2021 degree and work starting in 2020, and any "100% HIPAA / GxP / zero-leakage" guarantee. One 3.8 review says the rating would have been higher if risks had been stated in the proposal. Put limits in the proposal.

Proposals stay short, name a real system you have built, name two or three workflows from the post, state one risk, and offer one fixed first milestone. A human confirms every draft. Nothing auto-bids. Do not sell bidding from someone else's account.
A paid skills pack will not carry income. Build those files only when a client engagement needs them. Keep the Upwork MCP kit private this month.
Cash in week one is not a real target. After a client releases a fixed-price milestone, Upwork holds funds (the plans cite 5 days; hourly is slower). Confirm the current schedule in payment settings.
v2's $65 sticker beats v1's $85. Only 46 Claude-title hourly jobs allow $50 or more, and only 9 allow $100 or more. $65 is a search key for that band. Quoted prices are the packages.

item.claim: Keep $120 to $150 per hour and refuse work under a $3,000 floor, positioned as Enterprise AI Architect.
item.response: Reject this as the profile strategy. Nine Claude-title hourly jobs allow $100 or more. Visible hourly history tops out at $30. Gemini's overview repeats the unverifiable guarantee Claude correctly removes. A $3,000 minimum on day one fights both posted budgets and a Job Success score that a single large bad outcome can move.

item.claim: MCP boilerplates, LangGraph, and custom MCP servers are the catalog and the headline. Catalog cash arrives in 24 to 48 hours, and a $3,500 to $6,000 contract closes by day six.
item.response: Buyers in the observed posts want a workflow running, not a repository. Unassisted code is a refund risk. The day-five and day-six revenue assumes orders that do not exist yet and ignores the payment hold. Proposals about OAuth and SSE lose to proposals about the client's inbox, CRM, and docs.

item.claim: Consultations are off and should be $150 for 45 minutes. Client quality equals rating at least 4.8 and spend at least $1,000.
item.response: Claude v2, which read more of the account, says consultations are on and that one 30-minute call sold at $30. Trust that until the live page says otherwise. Spend of $1,000 does not filter out the $5.04-per-hour client. A 30-minute consultation at $75 is enough: bookable, and not a return to a $30 or $50 anchor. $150 recreates the $120 credibility gap.

item.claim: Set the profile rate to about $85 and send 4 to 6 proposals a day.
item.response: $85 still sits above almost every posted ceiling that has room left. The daily quota will force bids that fail the scorecard. On the counted day only 9 Claude-title jobs had fewer than 5 proposals and 35 had fewer than 10.

item.claim: Use the long keyword title "Claude AI Implementation | Claude Code, Skills & MCP | AI Agents & n8n Automation".
item.response: That line is about 80 characters. Confirm the title limit on the edit screen; expect something near 70. Use one outcome and two search terms: "Claude Code & AI Automation for Business Teams".

item.claim: Put n8n in the title because there are 204 n8n jobs.
item.response: Keep n8n as a skill and a search term. Fifty-four of the fixed-price n8n jobs are under $100. Leading with it pulls the cheap gigs that recreate the old rate history.

item.claim: Send 3 to 5 proposals a day, and price the starter at $299 because $251 receives a 1.25 Job Success weight.
item.response: After payment verified, hire rate, average pay of at least $25 per hour, nobody hired, a low proposal count, and a location you can accept, many days will have one or two real targets. Send those. Skip the quota. The 1.25 weight is a tie-break, not a pricing strategy. Charge $299 or $599 when the scope is setup, skills, a connector, and a recording. A tight $250 to $400 install is fine when that is the real scope. Do not take a $50 placeholder budget unless you re-quote and they accept.

item.claim: Message all five idle 2023–2024 contracts with a Claude sprint so a new payment trips the 90-day repeat-client rule.
item.response: v2 itself says that rule is a reading of the insights page and should be confirmed on one client first. Waking a dead scraping or fine-tune contract can produce a bad ending. Start with the enterprise client who already hired you several times. For the other open contracts, ask whether they want the work closed with feedback, and offer new work only when it continues what you already did for them.

item.claim: Week one includes a signed contract, a 12-to-20 skill kit, multiple catalog products, specialized profiles, and a proposal blitz.
item.response: There are 110 Connects. At 15 to 20 Connects a proposal, that is 5 to 7 submits. Catalog review is not instant. There is no Claude case study yet, and the proposal template depends on one. Specialized profiles wait until the main profile is converting. Buy Connects before applying. Leave profile boost off.

item.claim: Use the Top Rated feedback-removal perk on the 3.8-rated $4,408 WordPress contract now.
item.response: Those sub-5 ratings are outside the 24-month window, so they are not in the current score. Clients can still see them. Save the perk for a future in-window problem unless the perks page makes this removal free and unlimited.

item.claim: Outside agency blogs and skill-marketplace articles are enough to price a $1,000 to $2,500 care plan and to forecast kit revenue.
item.response: Those sources are too weak to set a retainer. Price a care plan after a client has finished a sprint. Do not build the Gumroad kit or a public proposal-engine product this month.

item.claim: Prefer any client with more than $1,000 spent, and personalize cover letters with names pulled from their reviews.
item.response: Average hourly rate paid replaces the spend rule. A light reference to a public review is enough. Building the letter around a scraped first name is a gimmick.

conflicts_to_confirm_live.conflict: Consultations: Gemini says off. Claude v2 says on, with one 30-minute call sold at $30 in 2025.
Proposal window: v1 says 0 sent in the last 3 months. v2 says 0 in the last 7 days and last activity about 3 months ago.
Recommended sticker: v1 says about $85, v2 says about $65, Gemini says keep $120 to $150. This analysis adopts $65.
Job Success 90-day and earnings-weight rules are taken from v2's reading of the insights page. Confirm the wording before using them.
Badge cost, Connects price, Freelancer Plus price, title character limit, and payment-hold length change. Read them on the account.

phase.name: Account and profile
phase.step: Confirm consultations, the 2026-08-31 invite, the five open contracts, Connects balance, badge cost, and the Job Success insights wording.
Set the title to a short line that fits the field. Recommended: Claude Code & AI Automation for Business Teams.
Set the profile rate to $65. Move it to $80 only after three completed contracts at the new level are visible. Do not change the rate inside a running contract.
Rewrite the first two lines: you set up Claude so a team uses it on their real tools, with skills, a handover, and a recording. Top Rated, 100% Job Success.
Delete the years claim and the compliance guarantee.
Add skill tags Upwork accepts: Claude, Claude Code, AI agents, automation, n8n, MCP, Python, API integration. Drop filler tags if the list is full. n8n stays a skill, not the title.
Turn the availability badge on. Decline the 2026-08-31 instructor invite unless pay and scope are specific and decent.
Buy Connects before applying. Freelancer Plus is worth it for this push if the current offer is still about $20 a month. Leave profile boost off.
Set a 30-minute consultation at $75 if consultations are part of the profile. Do not use $50 or $150.

phase.name: Proof and past clients
phase.step: Record one two-minute demo of Claude running one real workflow end to end. Put it in the portfolio. That demo is the proof sentence in every proposal.

Replace the OpenClaw catalog items with one listing: Claude Setup Sprint at $299 / $599 / $1,200. Submit the audit listing only after the sprint is in review. Leave MCP boilerplates and any $3,000 catalog item unpublished.
Message the repeat enterprise client with the sprint or a short audit, through the existing Upwork room. Then message past clients who left a clear 5.0, one offer each.
For the other idle contracts, ask whether they want the work closed with feedback. Offer new work only when it continues the original job.

phase.name: Proposals
phase.step: Reconnect the Upwork MCP server under the Aryan P. login before any live call. The plans warn that a previous session was authorized to a different account.
Use the MCP loop: jobs posted today, payment verified, then the full job record, then an invitation and existing-proposal check, then a draft, then human confirm.

Apply only when average hourly paid is at least $25, rating is at least 4.7 or the post is specific and new, hire rate is at least 50%, nobody is hired, proposals are still low, and the location does not exclude you.
The first offer on every new client is the sprint or a small audit. Implementation at $3,000 to $7,500 is for a client who has already finished one of those.
Read the draft, the bid, and the Connects cost, then confirm. Cap a day around 80 Connects. Stop boosting if a week of boosted proposals does not raise the view rate.
Do not build the Gumroad kit or the proposal-engine product this month. The MCP docs stay a private system.

how_to_judge.check: After 20 proposals, if fewer than about 6 were opened, change the first two lines and who you are targeting.
If proposals are opened and nobody replies, the proof or the first price is wrong.
A signed contract in week one is a good outcome, mostly if a past client says yes. It is not the bar for whether the week worked.
Cash follows the hold, so a milestone approved at the end of week one pays out the following week.
Month-one scoreboard from v2: a few sprints or audits and something like $2,500 to $7,000 contracted. Treat the top of that range as a stretch. These are planning numbers, not a forecast.
